meta.subject: Visa Seva / Indian Visa Online portal
meta.note_on_naming: There is no official product branded 'Visa Seva'. Public complaints refer to indianvisaonline.gov.in (e-Visa and regular visa). A separate MEA system called SEWA (indianconsularservices.mea.gov.in) is for consular services for Indians abroad and is not the same portal.
meta.limitation: All 37 unique supplied review URLs were checked in an interactive browser. Thirty-one were accessible, four regional Trustpilot URLs showed connection verification, Tripadvisor returned no usable page content, and the VisaHQ link returned a not-found page. Matching Trustpilot review cards on accessible listings were used to verify reviewer names and dates. Existing captured text is preserved where the original page could not be re-verified.
meta.how_to_read_text: Each record has a 'text' field with the complete captured body. Viral X threads also have 'thread_full_text' and 'thread_posts'. Trustpilot bodies are the complete sentences returned by public indexes; Trustpilot blocked live HTML (HTTP 403), so a few reviews may still be shorter than the live page if Trustpilot truncated the snippet.

refinement.content_policy: Existing captured text was preserved. Additional long verbatim third-party review text was not republished; browser verification was used to add metadata, provenance, accessibility status, and duplicate relationships.

data_quality_notes: Records 2 and 3 are excerpts from the same Trustpilot review.
Records 10 and 16 are excerpts from the same Trustpilot review.
Record 18 duplicates record 9 through a regional Trustpilot listing.
Trustpilot reviewer names and publication dates were corrected from visible review cards.
Month-only dates were retained where the source did not establish a precise day.

summary.overall_sentiment: Strongly negative on the application experience; more mixed after submission.
summary.headline: Applicants and X users describe indianvisaonline.gov.in as crashing, not saving form data, rejecting uploads, and taking hours or days. Viral posts (Raymond Russell, The Economist) amplified the same complaints. After submit, approvals are often fast.
dominant_complaint_themes: Form crashes or times out after clicking Next
Data not saved; users re-enter the same pages multiple times
Photo/passport upload rules are strict and error messages are unclear (JPEG vs PDF, file size)
Dated, desktop-first UI that is hard on mobile
Helpdesk replies described as generic or unhelpful
Workarounds: DuckDuckGo, Edge IE mode, off-peak hours, multiple devices

ux_vs_backend_vs_load.ux: Primary visible problem: multi-page forms, poor save/resume, picky uploads, confusing navigation.
ux_vs_backend_vs_load.backend: Crashes, timeouts, session drops, and payment retries indicate unstable session/server handling.
ux_vs_backend_vs_load.load: Steady international applicant stream rather than GST/ITR-style domestic peak; still enough concurrency that the stack appears fragile.

summary.traffic_context: Public search-traffic snapshots put official-site visits in the low-to-mid hundreds of thousands per month, not in India's top government-site tier (UIDAI/ECI/ITR). e-Visas are the majority of Indian visas issued.

reviews.title: Comically, profoundly, embarrassingly broken
reviews.text: Anybody who applies for an e-visa to India knows the website is always comically, profoundly, embarrassingly broken. It looks like it was written in 2003, kicks you out randomly without saving your work, won't charge your credit card until your nineteenth attempt. But this is a new one—halfway through the business visa application, it displays a list of the tallest peaks in each Indian state?? Come on folks, I'm just trying to invest in your country! I've always thought of the Indian e-visa website as a filtering test: if you can survive it, you'll be fine in India.

REPLY by @SanjayDani, 29 Jun 2026 [83 likes, 15,304 views]:
Used it two weeks ago.

(Airlines have stopped honoring valid PIO cards despite the PM’s assurance they’d be forever — and some of us don’t want dual citizenship for legal reasons, even if they claim it’s in name only. Story for another time.)

Four tries.

•Everything you type — and there’s a ton of it — randomly disappears.
•Cryptic red errors flag the wrong fields.
•It trips you on whether you were born in Pakistan.
•If I wasn’t a web hosting professional since the mid-90s I wouldn’t have cracked it in one sitting. This was designed by the dumbest primates to ever walk upright. Same degenerate soya-chunk brains you see on X daily. Not isolated.
•SBI payment is a masterclass in insularity. The rest of the world doesn’t use your in-country jugaad. No thank you.
•PayPal selection gets silently ignored, forcing you into SBI.
•If it wasn’t my 90-year-old mother waiting for me, I’d have turned back from Europe.

The designers, middlemen, and babus overseeing this website deserve physical torture. I’d plead guilty and sleep fine.

May you sadistic dumbasses burn in hell.
